subject: Resulting tree range pathology: tip ranges incorrect, range data shifted left by one

messages.author: 0622b2d732ce479e
messages.subject: Resulting tree range pathology: tip ranges incorrect, range data shifted left by one
parts:
Hello Nick and BioGeoBEARS users,

I am able to get BioGeoBEARS to run just fine, however my resulting output tree has a couple of strange issues:

1) The wrong ranges appear at the tips (based on the geography file, the current range data is shifted to the left by one). 

2) Taxa coded in the first geography range are shown as black on the mapped tree (as there was no further position left they appear black/blank?).

I had this results using my own data but also using the example Pyschotria data. I've attached my R script, examples of the geography files, as well as the resulting outputs.  

Thanks for any help or suggestions you can provide. 

Best,

Grey

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Resulting tree range pathology: tip ranges incorrect, range data shifted left by one
parts:
This is likely due to having changed something about the null range (0 areas).  The null range is the first range in the list of ranges/states, so if your likelihood analysis assumes the null range exists, but your graphing of the results assumes it doesn't, then everything would be shifted by 1. So, search your script on "include_null_range" and see if/where you've got this TRUE or FALSE (the defaults are TRUE, so start with that).

Cheers,
Nick
